If the extra days mean the Monday flight can't all go on the contract, book me whichever flight home it does cover. Economy.

must_keep.quote: 4.8 If a Supplier plans to spend personal time at the beginning or end of a business trip, they must inform the DBT Contract Manager. Additional costs must be covered by the Supplier if earlier or later return flights are more expensive than flights that would have been taken purely for the purposes of the business trip. Screenshots of the flights should be provided to evidence that the alternative flights/transport are not more expensive.
must_keep.why: personal time: tell the Contract Manager; the Supplier covers any extra fare over the flights purely for business

must_keep.quote: 1.14 If a Supplier plans to spend personal time at the beginning or end of a business trip, the DBT Contract Manager must be informed. All additional costs (travel, accommodation, subsistence) must be covered by the Supplier. The DBT Contract Manager will provide specific details on how to claim incurred expenses.
must_keep.why: personal time: the Contract Manager is informed and the Supplier covers extra costs

must_keep.quote: 4.6 Suppliers are expected to book the lowest logical fare available.
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest logical fare

design_notes: Lines 124-130: the Supplier covers extra cost only 'if earlier or later return flights are more expensive than flights that would have been taken purely for the purposes of the business trip'. The lowest Monday fare (JAL, 651.20) equals the lowest Friday fare (ANA, 651.20): not more expensive, so the leisure days add nothing and the Monday flight is booked. The Contract Manager has been told (lines 65-66).
